title: Grade 4 CREATIVE ARTS — Premium Revision Paper #6

pages.quiz:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6
====

GRADE: Grade 4
SUBJECT: CREATIVE ARTS
TIME ALLOWED: 120 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 100
ASSESSMENT: CBC school-based practice paper

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show your working and write the units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the one best answer.
4. Check your work before you hand in.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. Which twigs are best for making charcoal sticks? (1 mark)
   A. Wet, bent branches
   B. Green leaves
   C. Thick logs
   D. Dry, straight twigs about as thick as a pencil

2. Why must the tin of charcoal stay closed until it is cold? (1 mark)
   A. The charcoal will become white
   B. The tin will float
   C. Fresh air can make hot charcoal catch fire
   D. The charcoal will taste bad

3. Percussion instruments make sound when they are (1 mark)
   A. sung into
   B. bowed with a stick of hair
   C. blown with air only
   D. struck, shaken or scraped

4. What does the word indigenous mean? (1 mark)
   A. Very new
   B. Made in a factory
   C. Belonging to a people and place from long ago
   D. Brought from another continent

5. A full netball court is divided into how many equal parts? (1 mark)
   A. Two
   B. Three
   C. Four
   D. Six

6. To paint an object so it looks round, you should (1 mark)
   A. paint it black
   B. use one flat colour only
   C. paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   D. leave it blank

7. What is a good way to blend the edges of two tones? (1 mark)
   A. With sand
   B. With a dry stone
   C. With a knife
   D. With a damp brush

8. When darkening a colour with black, you should add (1 mark)
   A. a little at a time
   B. white first
   C. a whole tin at once
   D. nothing

9. Why is a pattern with only taa taa taa taa dull? (1 mark)
   A. It has too many rests
   B. It has no variation of note values
   C. It has no beat
   D. It is too long

10. Dictation in music means (1 mark)
   A. singing louder
   B. copying a friend's book
   C. writing down a pattern you hear
   D. drawing a picture

11. Which pattern has three beats of sound and one beat of silence? (1 mark)
   A. taa taa taa (rest)
   B. ta-te ta-te ta-te ta-te
   C. taa taa taa taa
   D. (rest) (rest) (rest) (rest)

12. What makes ending on d good for a short melody? (1 mark)
   A. It is the highest note
   B. It sounds finished and at rest
   C. It is the loudest note
   D. It sounds unfinished

13. Why should clay models dry slowly in the shade? (1 mark)
   A. Fast drying in strong sun can crack them
   B. Shade makes them heavy
   C. Sun makes them soft
   D. Shade makes them shine

14. Before joining a coil to a slab you should (1 mark)
   A. cover with oil
   B. paint them
   C. dry them in the sun
   D. scratch both and dab a little water

15. On the Kenyan flag, white stands for (1 mark)
   A. blood
   B. peace and honesty
   C. the people
   D. the sky

16. Where should you stay during a sprint race? (1 mark)
   A. Across all lanes
   B. In your own lane
   C. In any lane
   D. On the grass beside the track

17. Which part of the foot should touch the ground when sprinting? (1 mark)
   A. The ankle
   B. The front part of the foot
   C. The side only
   D. The heel

18. Which foot is usually placed in front at the start? (1 mark)
   A. Both together
   B. Neither
   C. The stronger foot, used to kick a ball
   D. The weaker foot always

19. Why is the national flag flown at national athletics events? (1 mark)
   A. It shows which country the athletes represent and builds pride
   B. To hide the track
   C. To block the wind
   D. To decorate only

20. What is a spotter or supporting partner's job? (1 mark)
   A. To laugh
   B. To help gently as your teacher shows you
   C. To push you
   D. To leave

21. In a side roll, you should keep your legs (1 mark)
   A. bent
   B. wide apart
   C. together with toes pointed
   D. lifted off the mat

22. What should you do with long hair in gymnastics? (1 mark)
   A. Cut it during class
   B. Tie it back
   C. Let it hang in your face
   D. Cover the mat with it

23. A sequence in gymnastics is (1 mark)
   A. a type of mat
   B. a single balance
   C. a set of movements performed in a fixed order
   D. a rule break

24. Which is a patriotic song? (1 mark)
   A. Kenya National Anthem
   B. A lullaby about sleeping
   C. A drum solo
   D. A hymn of worship only

25. Singing softly at the end of a lullaby shows (1 mark)
   A. a loud dynamic
   B. a high pitch only
   C. a fast tempo
   D. a soft dynamic

26. A sign that narrows to the right means (1 mark)
   A. getting faster
   B. getting softer
   C. repeat
   D. getting louder

27. A patriotic song shows (1 mark)
   A. a rainy day
   B. love for one's country
   C. love of sweets
   D. fear

28. Pitch is (1 mark)
   A. the words
   B. how high or low a note is
   C. how loud it is
   D. how fast it is

29. A topical song is (1 mark)
   A. about the moon only
   B. without a tune
   C. always sad
   D. about a topic that matters at a certain time

30. Which is good etiquette for a performer? (1 mark)
   A. Talk during the song
   B. Turn your back
   C. Walk on and off the stage quietly
   D. Push others

31. Before sharing a photograph of others, you should (1 mark)
   A. edit their face
   B. post it at once
   C. hide it
   D. ask them and an adult

32. After taking photos, choosing the best ones is called (1 mark)
   A. painting
   B. smudging
   C. hiding
   D. selecting

33. Indoors, the best place to stand for better light is (1 mark)
   A. in the cupboard
   B. in a dark corner
   C. near a window or open door
   D. under a table

34. Which is used only for taking photographs? (1 mark)
   A. Torch
   B. Radio
   C. Whistle
   D. Digital camera

35. Which note is played with the thumb and holes 1, 2 and 3 covered? (1 mark)
   A. A
   B. B
   C. G
   D. F

36. Where should you walk beside the pool? (1 mark)
   A. Jumping
   B. Running
   C. On the pool side, walking slowly
   D. Sliding

37. Floating means (1 mark)
   A. swimming fast
   B. sinking
   C. diving
   D. staying on top of the water without swimming

38. In the frog jump, you should land (1 mark)
   A. stiff
   B. softly with bent knees
   C. on your back
   D. on your head

39. Which Kiswahili word means frog? (1 mark)
   A. tembo
   B. kaa
   C. twiga
   D. chura

40. Which Kiswahili word means snake? (1 mark)
   A. kuku
   B. tumbili
   C. chura
   D. nyoka

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
41. Explain why covering more holes makes a lower note. (3 marks)

42. Name two digital devices used for taking photographs. (2 marks)

43. Give three hygiene rules for the pool. (3 marks)

44. Give four safety rules when making charcoal sticks. (4 marks)

45. State the three commands at the start of a sprint race in order. (2 marks)

46. Give one example of a melodic percussion instrument and one non-melodic percussion instrument. (2 marks)

47. What are indigenous games? (2 marks)

48. State four performance techniques for a good singer. (4 marks)

49. Name three water games and say how one is played. (3 marks)

50. State three mistakes in gliding and how to correct them. (3 marks)

51. Describe how to do the elephant walk. (3 marks)

52. Explain what a relay race is and how it teaches teamwork. (4 marks)

53. Describe how partners should give feedback on each other's gymnastics. (3 marks)

54. Explain how the elongated start is different from the medium start. (4 marks)

55. State the jobs of the lens, the screen and the battery of a camera. (3 marks)

56. Name the three joints of a descant recorder and state where the mouthpiece is. (3 marks)

57. What does giving with the ball mean in netball catching? (2 marks)

58. What is the centre of interest in a photograph? (3 marks)

59. Explain how you would learn a simple melody on B, A and G. (4 marks)

60. Describe how to make a value scale strip of orange. (3 marks)
pages.answers:
CREATIVE ARTS — PREMIUM REVISION PAPER #6 · MARKING SCHEME
====

SECTION A
----
1. D — Dry, straight twigs about as thick as a pencil
   Dry, straight, thin twigs burn evenly into good drawing sticks.

2. C — Fresh air can make hot charcoal catch fire
   Air can make hot charcoal burn, so we wait until it is fully cool.

3. D — struck, shaken or scraped
   A percussion instrument is played by hitting, shaking or scraping it.

4. C — Belonging to a people and place from long ago
   Indigenous instruments belong to a community and were made from local materials.

5. B — Three
   A netball court is divided into three equal thirds.

6. C — paint a lighter tone on the lit side and a darker tone on the shadow side
   Tones make an object look solid and round.

7. D — With a damp brush
   A damp brush joins the tones smoothly.

8. A — a little at a time
   Black is strong, so add it in small amounts.

9. B — It has no variation of note values
   A good pattern mixes different note values.

10. C — writing down a pattern you hear
   In dictation, the teacher plays or claps and you write it.

11. A — taa taa taa (rest)
   Only the first has a single rest and three sounding beats.

12. B — It sounds finished and at rest
   Ending on the home note gives a complete feeling.

13. A — Fast drying in strong sun can crack them
   Slow drying prevents cracks.

14. D — scratch both and dab a little water
   Scratching and wetting help the clay pieces stick.

15. B — peace and honesty
   White stands for peace and honesty.

16. B — In your own lane
   Running in your lane prevents crashes.

17. B — The front part of the foot
   Sprinters land on the balls of the feet.

18. C — The stronger foot, used to kick a ball
   The stronger foot is the front foot.

19. A — It shows which country the athletes represent and builds pride
   The flag is a symbol of the country.

20. B — To help gently as your teacher shows you
   A partner supports carefully and only in the way taught.

21. C — together with toes pointed
   Legs stay together to keep the log shape.

22. B — Tie it back
   Tied-back hair does not get in your way.

23. C — a set of movements performed in a fixed order
   A sequence links skills one after the other.

24. A — Kenya National Anthem
   The anthem is a patriotic song.

25. D — a soft dynamic
   Softness is dynamics.

26. B — getting softer
   A closing sign means the music grows softer.

27. B — love for one's country
   Patriotic songs celebrate the nation.

28. B — how high or low a note is
   Accurate pitch means singing the right notes.

29. D — about a topic that matters at a certain time
   Topical songs give messages about topics such as health, safety or the environment.

30. C — Walk on and off the stage quietly
   Good manners show respect for the audience and others.

31. D — ask them and an adult
   Respect and safety come first.

32. D — selecting
   Selecting means choosing the best.

33. C — near a window or open door
   Daylight helps.

34. D — Digital camera
   A digital camera is made for photography.

35. C — G
   G adds the third hole.

36. C — On the pool side, walking slowly
   Wet floors are slippery.

37. D — staying on top of the water without swimming
   Floating is resting on the surface.

38. B — softly with bent knees
   Bent knees absorb the shock.

39. D — chura
   Chura is a frog.

40. D — nyoka
   Nyoka is a snake.

SECTION B
----
41. (3 marks)
   Answer: The column of air inside becomes longer, and a longer air column vibrates more slowly, giving a lower note.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for longer air column, 2 marks for lower note.

42. (2 marks)
   Answer: Smartphone, tablet, digital camera. Any two.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

43. (3 marks)
   Answer: Shower before and after; do not spit or pass urine in the pool; do not drink the water; dry yourself and change into dry clothes. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

44. (4 marks)
   Answer: An adult does the burning; keep far from the fire; leave the tin closed until cold; collect only dead twigs; wash hands afterwards. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct rule.

45. (2 marks)
   Answer: On your marks, set, go.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for all three, 1 mark for the correct order.

46. (2 marks)
   Answer: Melodic: xylophone. Non-melodic: shaker, kayamba or claves.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each correct example.

47. (2 marks)
   Answer: Traditional games that belong to a people and were passed on from long ago.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

48. (4 marks)
   Answer: Good posture; deep breathing; clear diction; gestures; facial expression; eye contact. Any four.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

49. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bubble blowing, treasure hunt, follow the leader, water tag, circle walk. One correct explanation.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark each for three games, or 1 mark each for two games and an explanation.

50. (3 marks)
   Answer: Lifting the head: keep it between the arms; bent arms or legs: stretch them; pushing too hard: push gently. Any three.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

51. (3 marks)
   Answer: Bend forward at the waist, clasp hands so that the arms hang like a trunk, and walk slowly with heavy steps, swaying the trunk.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

52. (4 marks)
   Answer: A relay is a race in which each runner in a team runs a short distance and passes a baton to the next runner. The team wins by working together and passing smoothly.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for team running, 1 mark for the baton, 2 marks for teamwork explanation.

53. (3 marks)
   Answer: Watch carefully, say one good thing first, then one thing to improve, and be kind.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each point.

54. (4 marks)
   Answer: The rear knee is placed further back, level with the heel of the front foot. The feet are further apart. The push is longer and stronger but may feel less steady.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each valid difference or explanation, up to 4.

55. (3 marks)
   Answer: The lens lets light in; the screen shows the view and photos; the battery gives power.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each.

56. (3 marks)
   Answer: Head joint, middle joint and foot joint. The mouthpiece is on the head joint.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the joints, 1 mark for order or naming all, 1 mark for the mouthpiece.

57. (2 marks)
   Answer: Bending the arms as the ball arrives so as to take the force out of it.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for bending arms, 1 mark for softening the catch.

58. (3 marks)
   Answer: The main subject that you want the viewer to notice first, for example a friend's face or a flower.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for main subject, 1 mark for noticed first, 1 mark for an example.

59. (4 marks)
   Answer: Sing it in sol-fa, clap and say the rhythm, finger the notes without blowing, play slowly, then speed up keeping the beat steady.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for each step.

60. (3 marks)
   Answer: Draw a strip and divide it into five boxes. Mix orange with white for the two light boxes. Paint pure orange in the middle. Mix orange with black for the two dark boxes.
   Working / marking points: 1 mark for the five boxes, 1 mark for light tones, 1 mark for dark tones.
